question: A 71-year-old man presented with severe pancytopenia without any immature cells and with a medullar study suggestive of severe aplastic anemia. What would be the fundamental therapeutic approach?

options.opa: Treatment with methylprednisolone at a dose of 1 g / Kg / day for 5 days.
options.opb: Study of siblings and if any is HLA compatible, allogeneic transplant of hemopoietic progenitors.
options.opc: Immunosuppressive therapy with cyclosporine and antitimocitic immunoglobulin.
options.ope: Chemotherapy and if autologous transplant response of hemopoietic progenitors.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Severe pancytopenia -> Medullar study suggestive of severe aplastic anemia -> Fundamental therapeutic approach -> 70% CHAIN: Severe aplastic anemia -> Bone marrow failure -> Hemopoietic progenitor transplant -> 80% CHAIN: Hemopoietic progenitor transplant -> Study of siblings for HLA compatibility -> Allogeneic transplant -> 75% CHAIN: Severe aplastic anemia -> Immunosuppressive therapy -> Cyclosporine and antithymocyte immunoglobulin -> 70%
analysis: Severe aplastic anemia is a condition characterized by pancytopenia and hypocellular bone marrow. The fundamental therapeutic approach involves immunosuppressive therapy to halt the immune-mediated destruction of hematopoietic stem cells.
